eventMetadata.context_description: Recent forecasts from the UK Met Office show a high-pressure system centered over southern England driving a modest southerly flow that supports a London maximum near 20°C today, explaining why this outcome leads trader consensus at 41.5% implied probability. Ensemble guidance clusters tightly between 19–21°C because partial cloud cover and moderate winds are expected to moderate peak heating while preventing stronger warming. Current conditions sit slightly above the long-term May average of 18°C, with no signals of an anomalous heat plume. Traders are watching afternoon surface observations and any late model adjustments, as shifts in insolation or boundary-layer mixing could readily move implied odds toward the 19°C or 21°C brackets.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent Hong Kong Observatory and multi-model consensus forecasts indicate a daytime maximum near 28–29°C for May 21, driven by a weakening monsoon flow and increasing southerly moisture that favors partly cloudy skies with scattered showers. This keeps surface temperatures close to the long-term May average while limiting strong daytime heating, which explains why the market assigns the highest probabilities to 28°C and 29°C. Key differentiating factors include the timing and coverage of afternoon convection, which can shave 1–2°C off the peak, versus clearer intervals that allow brief warming toward 30°C. With the event only hours away, traders are watching the latest 12–24 hour model runs for any shift in cloud or wind patterns that could alter the final observed maximum at the official recording station.
